promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 6 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Your fitness is clearly there, but 53 miles and a 20-miler was a jump of more than 40 percent in a single week. This week drops to 39 miles so your body can absorb that before we build again.

answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer:
You can't keep this up yet, and adding more won't help. You ran 53 miles against 38 planned, up from 37 the week before. You also stretched the long run from 14 to 20 miles.

Feeling fine right now is normal. Your heart and lungs adapt within days. Tendons, bones and calves take weeks, so overload often shows up one to three weeks later.

Your right knee complained a month ago at only 32 miles a week, and your calves were tight on Sunday night. That's why this week comes down to 39 miles. Over the following weeks the plan builds back into the mid-40s.

Treat each planned distance as the most you run that day, not the least. Finishing a run feeling great means the training is working. Save that energy for the next session rather than spending it on extra miles.

new.analysis:
## How the week went

The running itself was excellent. Your easy runs stayed at 9:50/mi and heart rate 139, the same as before the heat. Your four threshold reps held 7:55/mi without slowing at all.

The problem was how much you ran. Every run went past the plan, and Monday's rest day became a run.

| Day | Planned | Ran |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mon Sep 7 | rest | 4 mi easy |
| Tue Sep 8 | 6 mi easy | 7 mi |
| Wed Sep 9 | 8 mi, 3 x 1.5 mi at 8:00/mi | 9 mi, 4 x 1.5 mi at 7:55/mi |
| Thu Sep 10 | 5 mi easy | 7 mi |
| Fri Sep 11 | rest | rest |
| Sat Sep 12 | 4 mi easy | 6 mi |
| Sun Sep 13 | 15 mi easy, heart rate under 150 | 20 mi, average heart rate 149 |
| Total | 38 mi | 53 mi |

## Why Sunday matters most

Sunday's 20 miles gave you two hard days in the week instead of one. It took 3 h 20 min, spent 88 percent of the time in zone 3 and felt like effort 7/10. That makes it closer to a long steady effort than an easy long run.

That run is also why only 54 percent of your week counted as easy by heart rate. Your easy runs were 97 to 98 percent in zone 2, so almost all the gap came from Sunday.

At your long-run pace, running past about 3 hours costs more recovery than it adds in fitness. From here your long runs top out around 18 miles. The gains will come from adding marathon pace, not more distance.

## Why this week is lighter

At 39 miles, this week is still bigger than any week before last week. It gives your legs time to catch up with the 53 rather than stacking another big week on top. The threshold session is the same size as last week's plan, so you keep that fitness.

Keep doing both hip and glute sessions. They're the main thing that settled your knee in August.

## The weeks ahead

Over the next three weeks the plan builds into the mid-40s. Your Sunday long runs will include miles at marathon pace, 8:35/mi, and you'll add a longer run of 9 to 10 miles during the week. The taper starts in mid-October. Each of those weeks only works if you stick to the planned distances.
